- `0a3013221a215aa2` [general] No single primary study directly A/Bs selective retrieval vs summary vs compression vs full-context and reports token savings as the outcome metric for long-running agents was found; each source reports a different metric (accuracy at fixed context, context-window multiplier, compression ratio, per-call context bounds). Settling evidence would be a controlled experiment on a long-running agent benchmark (e.g., SWE-bench agentic runs or long-horizon tool use) measuring billed input tokens and task success across the four arms with identical model and task; to the reviewer's knowledge no such published benchmark exists.

- `0b44c39d153c71e2` [general] A biologically-grounded agent memory architecture combines sleep-phase consolidation, interference-based forgetting, engram maturation, reconsolidation upon retrieval, entity knowledge graphs, and hybrid multi-cue retrieval; deduplication-based consolidation achieved 97.2% retention precision with 58% store reduction (+21.8 pp over baseline). Source: 'Human-Inspired Memory Architecture for LLM Agents', arXiv 2605.08538.

- `7c0a290e885b0a7d` [general] Agent memory systems almost universally keep the long-term fact store append-only and unbounded, solving 'growth' by bounding only the in-context tier and by re-ranking/superseding at retrieval: MemGPT/Letta evicts the context queue to a recursive summary while archival/recall storage grows indefinitely; decay exists as a retrieval-time ranking bias and never deletes; dedup is write-time; invalidation/supersede is timestamp-based and non-destructive; per-item expiry exists as soft-hide (Mem0 expiration_date) and is absent from LangGraph's core store.

- `2bc3ff3548b14a6f` [general] Verdict synthesis: DMR (MemGPT, 2023) measures single-session-hop fact recall on short 5-session MSC chats and is near-saturated (full-context baseline matches the memory system); LoCoMo (2024) measures long-horizon QA across single/multi-hop, temporal, open-domain, and adversarial questions plus event-summarization, with temporal reasoning and abstention the hardest axes (human 87.9 F1 vs. best model ~37.8; long-context adversarial 2.1%); LongMemEval (ICLR 2025) explicitly measures IE, MR, TR, KU, ABS at 115k–1.5M-token scales, documenting 30–60% drops for long-context LLMs and 37–64% drops for commercial memory assistants.

Source: arXiv:2501.13956, Tables 1-3.

- `f799ae94c5278f06` [general] Anthropic's engineering blog 'Effective context engineering for AI agents' (2025) asserts that giving the model less context is generally better: every unneeded token is both a confusion risk and a budget waste. Core techniques are context narrowing (retrieval pulling only relevant snippets), dynamic context assembly per call, entity memory/scratchpads, and summarization (a separate compression category for high-level understanding only). It warns against dumping full call transcripts into subagent calls. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-agents

- `e368dbd927efdfc0` [general] MemGPT (Packer et al., arXiv:2310.08560, 2023) reports handling contexts exceeding the LLM context window by a factor of 10 while maintaining performance on dialogue and document analysis tasks, via OS-inspired tiered memory (main/external context) with selective retrieval ('paging'). - `8baa3b2f82d7faa6` [general] Opinion (sourced inference, not a measured study): the selector for agents is which failure you must survive and at what cost — WAL+checkpoint gives strongest crash consistency and minimal replay but needs a storage-engine contract and is overkill for small agent state; snapshot-restore is simplest with a bounded recovery window but loses everything since the last snapshot unless combined with a log (RPO = snapshot interval); event sourcing enables exact resume, audit, time travel, and human-in-the-loop review at the cost of side-effect duplication, unbounded history requiring compaction/pruning, and schema/version evolution of events.

- `672b4912c42144b2` [general] DMR measures single-session-hop fact recall (opinion grounded in source): whether an agent can pull one specific fact out of a prior session; it tests retrieval/consistency, not updating, temporal reasoning, or abstention. Zep's primary text criticizes it: 'The evaluation relies exclusively on single-turn, fact-retrieval questions... Each conversation contains only 60 messages, easily fitting within current LLM context windows.'

- `3b3bae3fd783ee40` [general] Uncertain/estimated: RoMem's cross-benchmark numbers use a different metric than the original LoCoMo paper (Recall@10 over ~1,986 QA pairs vs. the original paper's F1 answer prediction over 50 dialogues); LoCoMo question count differs across sources (1,813 in one 2026 paper vs. 1,986 in RoMem). Zep's LongMemEval improvements (up to +18.5% accuracy, −90% latency) are vendor self-reported. No primary source reached gives a controlled head-to-head of a 'pure' append-only store vs. an updating store on all three benchmarks with an identical LLM judge.

- `832a7c538944c10a` [general] Cross-benchmark retrieval numbers are not comparable; each row's comparison is only valid within its own benchmark/model. A single head-to-head benchmark running all five retrieval strategies (BM25, dense, recency-aware, entity graph, hybrids) on the same agent-memory QA set with the same reader LLM does not yet exist in peer-reviewed sources; LongMemEval's retriever ablation (Table 9) is the closest existing partial comparison.

- `7d97975df00109c5` [general] LLMLingua (Jiang et al., Microsoft, EMNLP 2023, arXiv:2310.05736) reports coarse-to-fine prompt compression achieving a ratio up to 20x with minimal performance loss (budgets 1x/3x/5x/10x/20x), with measured savings in compressed token count and FLOPs reduction. - `8742eae87151033d` [general] A position paper argues current agent memory (vector stores, RAG, scratchpads) implements lookup, not memory: drawing on Complementary Learning Systems theory, biological intelligence pairs fast hippocampal exemplar storage with slow neocortical weight consolidation, and current AI agents implement only the first half. Source: 'Contextual Agentic Memory is a Memo, Not True Memory', arXiv 2604.27707.

Source: arXiv:2501.13956, Table 3.

- `50662f026de1acfe` [general] Embedding-based retrieval alone does not close the gap to human fact recall in long conversations: on LongMemEval even commercial memory chatbots with dense memory (ChatGPT GPT-4o 57.7%, Coze 33.0%) drop 37% and 64% vs offline reading of full context (91.8%). Source: arXiv:2410.10813v2, Figure 3a.

- `40a6f5c1783caef7` [general] OpenAI Agents SDK session guide assigns: SQLiteSession to local development and simple apps, AsyncSQLiteSession to async dev, RedisSession to shared session memory across multiple workers or services, SQLAlchemySession to production apps with existing databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, etc.), MongoDBSession to multi-process horizontally-scalable session storage, and DaprSession to production cloud-native deployments; the documented production path for concurrent workers is a shared-server DB or a single long-running app server that serializes access, not a shared SQLite file.

- `4a16c7ba303c62e7` [general] RecMem keeps incoming interactions in a 'subconscious' embedding layer and invokes the LLM to extract episodic/semantic memory only on sustained recurrence of semantically similar interactions; it reduced memory-construction token cost of three SOTA memory systems by up to 87% while exceeding their accuracy. Source: ACL 2026 Findings, arXiv 2605.16045.

- `90b6a3e4a78524a2` [general] MemGPT (arXiv:2310.08560 §2.2) queue manager enforces a warning token count (e.g. 70% of context window) that inserts a system 'memory pressure' warning so the LLM can move data to working context or archival storage, and a flush token count (e.g. 100%) at which it evicts a count of messages (e.g. 50% of context window) and generates a new recursive summary from the existing recursive summary plus evicted messages; the FIFO queue's first slot holds that recursive summary.

- `9cc983109ba5b4f3` [general] CoALA never uses the term 'consolidation' — verified in full text; the concept maps to three distinct mechanisms: per-agent reflection written back to semantic memory (Reflexion/Generative Agents), save-time pipeline dedup (CrewAI), and background system-owned consolidation (Mem0 Dream). [fact]

- `9fd0d62f3cea36ac` [general] DMR (Deep Memory Retrieval) is a task introduced in the MemGPT paper, built on the Multi-Session Chat (MSC) dataset; the agent is asked a question referring back to a prior conversation with a very narrow expected answer range, with QA pairs generated by a separate LLM instructed to write questions answerable only from the old chat log and not contained in persona information.

- `e286837b45d310e8` [general] Static-dynamic dilemma (RoMem primary text): 'most existing approaches model time as discrete metadata, either sorting by recency (burying old-yet-permanent knowledge), simply overwriting outdated facts, or requiring an expensive LLM call at every ingestion step, leaving them unable to distinguish persistent facts from evolving ones.' Failure directions: recency sorting silently buries static knowledge (decades-old fact ranked below fresher irrelevant entries); disabling recency bias leaves temporal conflicts unresolved, confusing the downstream LLM. RoMem asserts its append-only store works only because contradictions are resolved geometrically at query time, and claims all existing baselines (Mem0, Zep, LicoMemory, HippoRAG) treat memory as a static snapshot, causing contradictory facts to cluster together in retrieval space and confuse the LLM.

- `9a057f6afaa72539` [general] D-MEM decouples short-term interaction from cognitive restructuring via Fast/Slow routing on Reward Prediction Error: routine low-RPE inputs bypass or cache in an O(1) buffer, high-RPE inputs (factual contradictions, preference shifts) trigger the O(N) memory-evolution pipeline; reduces token consumption over 80% and removes the O(N^2) write-latency bottleneck of append-and-evolve systems like A-MEM. Source: arXiv 2603.14597.

- `ca8c6940f3cb0005` [general] RecMem (arXiv:2605.16045, ACL 2026 Findings) frames the core dichotomy in LLM memory consolidation: existing systems invoke LLMs to process every incoming interaction for memory extraction ('eager consolidation'), which leads to substantial token consumption; RecMem's fix triggers LLM consolidation only when semantically similar interactions recur (thresholds theta_sim=0.6-0.7, theta_count=4-5), buffering everything else in an embedding-only 'subconscious' store.

- `faedc0f0a4b0184b` [general] Consolidation rewrites hedged/casual statements into confident dated assertions the agent treats as verified facts; the agent responds to phrasing confidence, not source; a passive 'unverified' tag is ignored, while keeping tentative phrasing rather than upgrading it is the store-level fix; a single redundant source restores correct decisions. Source: 'Manufactured Confidence', arXiv 2606.29279.

- `0b6bcd41fb0c4fef` [general] Retrieval reading strategy is a separate measurable lever: LongMemEval, even with perfect retrieval, Chain-of-Note + structured data format improves QA accuracy by as much as 10 absolute points across three LLMs; on LongMemEvalS long-context LLMs drop 30-60% vs oracle retrieval. Source: arXiv:2410.10813v2, Section 5.5 + Figure 3b.

- `9807eb38133c8148` [general] Generative Agents (arXiv:2304.03442 §4.1) retrieval score = alpha_recency*recency + alpha_importance*importance + alpha_relevance*relevance with all alpha = 1; recency is an exponential decay over sandbox game hours since last retrieval (decay factor 0.995); importance is an LLM-assigned 1-10 integer at creation; every memory object carries creation and most-recent-access timestamps; the memory stream is unbounded and decay only re-ranks at retrieval.

- `a668572194f1c30e` [general] The TMLR survey 'A Survey of Agent Memory in the Second Half' reports hundreds of agent-memory papers in 2025 and frames memory as the substrate of self-evolution: short-term memory gates which experiences are abstracted, long-term memory consolidates them into reusable knowledge and skills, and memory management itself is becoming a trainable capability. Source: arXiv 2602.06052.

- `075b797922584daa` [general] GAM explicitly decouples memory encoding from consolidation: ongoing dialogue lives in an event-progression graph and is integrated into a topic-associative network only on semantic shifts, minimizing interference while preserving long-term consistency (SOTA on LoCoMo and LongDialQA). Source: arXiv 2604.12285.

- `70d2e0f66bef8b38` [general] Zep/Graphiti (arXiv:2501.13956 §2.2.3) uses a bi-temporal model: timeline T (when a fact holds) and T' (transactional ingestion), each edge storing t_valid, t_invalid, t'_created, t'_expired; an LLM compares new edges against semantically related existing edges for contradictions and invalidates temporally overlapping affected edges by setting t_invalid to the invalidating edge's t_valid; Graphiti prioritizes new information; retrieval returns the t_valid/t_invalid range so stale-but-historical facts remain representable.

- `8af8f2689671ac0a` [evidence-status] Cross-framework comparison: mini-agi (verify_command/verify_target exit-code gate, outcome.achieved as run's own claim, unverified without gate, disagrees -> exit 1 + gap held + judge-drift calibration); SWE-bench (FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS in Docker, patch is the artifact, no self-report, wrong-but-green patches the open failure mode); Terminal-Bench/Harbor (test.sh -> reward file, separate verifier env, tamper-sensitive evidence via sidecars); Claude Code (user-supplied check, Stop hook blocks turn with 8-block override, fresh subagent refutes); OpenAI Evals (deterministic comparators, LLM grades own output, D/E labels); Voyager/Reflexion/LATS (self-critique is the loop's own feedback signal, no separate judge).

- `19ef42b700d36e05` [general] RecMem quality: selective batch consolidation matches or beats eager systems on accuracy — best overall among memory-based methods on both benchmarks (LoCoMo GPT-4.1-mini: 81.10 vs Mem0 62.92 / A-Mem 68.83; LongMemEval-S: 76.80 vs 71.20 / 71.60, and beats FullContext 66.20); but on short LoCoMo conversations FullContext still slightly outperforms RecMem (76.43 vs 72.47, gpt-4o-mini), i.e. the consolidation saving is not free on small contexts (RecMem Tables 1-2).

- `68944cdb3db0a2fc` [general] Retrieval techniques are complements, not alternatives — the biggest gains come from stacking them: Zep = temporal KG + hybrid lexical/dense/graph retrieval; HippoRAG = KG + embeddings + PPR; LongMemEval's best config = session decomposition + fact-augmented keys + time-aware query expansion. Sources: arXiv:2501.13956; arXiv:2405.14831; arXiv:2410.10813v2.

- `77e29c7c6707642d` [general] TrustMem verifies each memory-update transition on coverage, preservation, and faithfulness via a Memory Transition Verifier, then uses preference-pair RL over candidate updates; it reduced transition-level omission, corruption, and hallucination by 40.1%, 79.1%, and 50.0% respectively versus strongest per-error baselines. Source: arXiv 2606.25161.

- `a7ce42ab7d93d083` [general] OpenAI Agents SDK guardrails have three layers: input (on first-agent input, parallel or blocking), output (on final output), and tool guardrails (input checks before a function-tool runs — can skip, replace output, or raise a tripwire; output checks after); tripwires raise exceptions and halt the run; ordering vs approvals is configurable via `ToolExecutionConfig(pre_approval_tool_input_guardrails=True)`; tool guardrails apply only to `function_tool` tools, not hosted/built-in tools or handoffs.

- `6977145a51d83491` [general] Hybrid LLM routing value depends sharply on the model-pair quality gap: at a 20% cost advantage the small-gap pair (Llama-2 7b/13b) loses <=0.1% BART quality, the large-gap pair (FLAN-t5 800m/Llama-2 13b) loses up to 5.8%. When the gap is large, training on Pr[H>=0] labels is near-useless ('0 for almost 90% of queries'); a label-relaxation transformation (Pr[H>=−t]) recovers a usable signal. (Hybrid LLM, arXiv 2404.14618v1, Table 1, §3.3, Fig 4a)

- `74a333f06b0e1b1b` [general] Recurring across independent LLM-routing papers: (1) the achievable tradeoff is dominated by the size of the weak/strong quality gap and the training-data distribution match (augmentation and low-data regimes matter more than router architecture); (2) routers over-deploy the strong model in practice (RouterArena normalized deferral curve), so the frontier is far from the oracle; (3) router overhead itself is measurable and non-trivial (latency, embedding API calls, per-request cost) but small vs generation cost.

- `8eff920971cc7319` [general] Claude Code hooks fire per session (`SessionStart`/`SessionEnd`), per turn (`UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`), and on every tool call (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, plus `PermissionRequest`/`PermissionDenied`); handlers can be shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tools, LLM prompts, or subagents; `matcher` (tool name/regex) + `if` (permission-rule syntax) filter them; MCP tools match as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`; hooks can return `permissionDecision: 'deny'` to block a call; hooks live in settings files, managed policy, plugin `hooks/hooks.json`, or skill/agent frontmatter; `allowManagedHooksOnly` lets enterprises suppress user/project/plugin hooks.

- `d86f43007ae0e974` [general] The SQLite wal-index is backed by a file mmapped in the same directory as the database; processes with a different root directory (via chroot) will see different files and use different shared memory areas, leading to database corruption — a chroot'd sandbox worker cannot reliably share a WAL-mode store on the same filesystem path.

- `e232f1c2ce57f2cf` [general] MCP enforced contract: `inputSchema` MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (2020-12 default); `outputSchema` is optional but binding when present (servers MUST provide conforming structured results, clients SHOULD validate); tool annotations from non-trusted servers MUST be considered untrusted; servers MUST validate all inputs, enforce access controls, rate-limit, and sanitize outputs; clients SHOULD validate tool results before handing them to the LLM; there SHOULD be a human able to deny invocations; SEP-1303 routes input-validation failures into the `isError: true` tool-result channel.
